newsitem.title: USA: UN okays 37th Iraq oil contract, first period over.
newsitem.headline: UN okays 37th Iraq oil contract, first period over.

text.p: U.N. overseers have approved a 37th Iraqi oil contract for lifting crude in the second period of the six-month oil-for-food accord, effectively ending first 90-day sales, U.N. officials said Friday.
The latest contract, like the previous 36th sale, will fall under the March 9-June 10 period of the oil deal.

"That will be all for the first period," said a Western diplomat. U.N. officials had said earlier on Friday that only a drastic decline in oil prices would have freed overseers to approve any additional sales for the first 90 days.
Now that the markets are closed, and prices failed to fluctuate widely, the first period was called complete.

U.N. officials said on Thursday that first period sales were extremely close, if not at, the $1 billion limit. The limit was actually $1.07 billion, which included a $70-million fee for using the Turkish pipeline.
Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude from the start of the deal on December 10 to June 10, but terms of the accord demand $1 billion be sold in each of the 90 days.
U.N. officials said the 36th and 37th contracts totalled 1.5 million barrels of oil, with the 37th contract thought to be for 600,000 barrels.
The 36th contract called for lifting 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) over 90 days, to tally at 900,000 barrels total.
There was some confusion on the companies involved in the last deals.

The United Nations, however, did state that all of the contracts approved thus far total 104 million barrels of Iraqi crude. There was no breakdown between 90-day periods for the volumes, but a more detailed account on volumes and oil receipts was to be released on Monday, officials said.
